business_summary.text: Graphite India is the largest Indian producer of graphite electrodes, with 80,000 tonnes per annum capacity across Durgapur and Nashik, plus a specialty graphite facility in Nurnberg, Germany.

call_points.text: No numeric FY27 guidance; management says it remains optimistic about improving realisations to absorb cost increases.
First phase of electrode capacity expansion expected to be commissioned in the current financial year.
FY26 sales grew 11.4% to ₹2,852 Cr on higher volumes with realisations flat.
Ongoing conflicts in West Asia continue to impact logistics and freight costs and have led to rationing of certain energy-based inputs.
Board recommended a dividend of ₹7 per share for FY2026, subject to shareholders' approval.

operating_notes.text: Graphite India increased its stake in GrafTech International Ltd to 9.79% with a further investment of ₹62.25 Cr, taking cumulative investment to ₹230.38 Cr.
FY26 capacity utilisation rose to 104% from 81% in Q4FY25.
FY26 sales growth was driven by higher volumes with realisations flat.
Inventory write-down to NRV was ₹47 Cr at 31 Mar 2026, down from ₹113 Cr at 31 Mar 2025.
Graphite India increased its stake in Godi India Private Limited to 52.68% from 45.76% via a rights issue subscription of ₹58.71 Cr, turning it into a subsidiary.

timeline.summary: Graphite India increased its shareholding in GrafTech International Ltd to 9.79% with an investment of ₹62.25 Cr.
Graphite India's FY26 earnings presentation showed consolidated net sales of ₹2,852 Cr (+11.4% YoY) and a Q4 net loss of ₹105 Cr including a ₹242 Cr fair-value loss on investments.
Graphite India invested ₹58.71 Cr in Godi India's rights issue to raise its stake from 45.76% to 52.68%, making it a subsidiary.
